Let \(V^{\otimes 3}\) have pure tensors written \(u\otimes v\otimes w\). First we determine all natural endomorphisms of \(T\).

For any permutation \(\sigma\in S_3\), the map
\[
P_\sigma(u_1\otimes u_2\otimes u_3)=u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes u_{\sigma(2)}\otimes u_{\sigma(3)}
\]
is natural, so every element of the group algebra \(\mathbb F_2[S_3]\) gives a natural endomorphism.

Conversely, let \(E:T\Rightarrow T\) be natural. Take \(W=\mathbb F_2^3\) with basis \(e_1,e_2,e_3\), and write
\[
E_W(e_1\otimes e_2\otimes e_3)
=
\sum_{a,b,c\in\{1,2,3\}} \lambda_{abc}\, e_a\otimes e_b\otimes e_c.
\]
If \(\pi_i:W\to W\) kills \(e_i\) and fixes the other two basis vectors, then
\[
\pi_i^{\otimes 3}(e_1\otimes e_2\otimes e_3)=0,
\]
so naturality gives
\[
\pi_i^{\otimes 3}E_W(e_1\otimes e_2\otimes e_3)=0.
\]
Thus every surviving term must contain \(i\). This holds for \(i=1,2,3\), so any nonzero coefficient must have \(\{a,b,c\}=\{1,2,3\}\). Hence
\[
E_W(e_1\otimes e_2\otimes e_3)
=
\sum_{\sigma\in S_3} c_\sigma\,
e_{\sigma(1)}\otimes e_{\sigma(2)}\otimes e_{\sigma(3)}.
\]
For arbitrary \(u,v,w\in V\), apply naturality to the linear map \(W\to V\) sending \(e_1,e_2,e_3\) to \(u,v,w\). Therefore every natural endomorphism is exactly an element of \(\mathbb F_2[S_3]\).

So we must count idempotents in \(\mathbb F_2[S_3]\).

Let \(r=(123)\), \(s=(12)\), so \(srs=r^{-1}\). In characteristic \(2\), define
\[
e_0=1+r+r^2,\qquad e_1=r+r^2.
\]
These are central orthogonal idempotents with \(e_0+e_1=1\). Therefore
\[
\mathbb F_2[S_3]\cong e_0\mathbb F_2[S_3]\times e_1\mathbb F_2[S_3].
\]

The first factor is
\[
e_0\mathbb F_2[S_3]\cong \mathbb F_2[C_2].
\]
Its elements are \(a+bt\) with \(t^2=1\). Since the characteristic is \(2\),
\[
(a+bt)^2=a+b.
\]
For this to equal \(a+bt\), we need \(b=0\), so this factor has exactly \(2\) idempotents.

For the second factor, \(e_1\mathbb F_2[S_3]\cong M_2(\mathbb F_2)\). Indeed, it is the skew group algebra \(\mathbb F_4\rtimes \operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_4/\mathbb F_2)\), which acts faithfully on \(\mathbb F_4\) as a \(2\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-vector space, hence is \(M_2(\mathbb F_2)\).

Now count idempotents in \(M_2(\mathbb F_2)\). An idempotent matrix is a projection, so
\[
\mathbb F_2^2=\operatorname{im} P\oplus \ker P.
\]
There is \(1\) idempotent of rank \(0\), \(1\) of rank \(2\), and for rank \(1\), there are \(3\) choices for the image line and \(2\) choices for a complementary kernel line. Thus
\[
1+3\cdot 2+1=8
\]
idempotents in \(M_2(\mathbb F_2)\).

Hence the total number is
\[
2\cdot 8=16.
\]

\[
\boxed{16}
\]
